bull_bear.body:
- "LAKSHYA RISE 5000" targets by FY 2029-30: revenue of ₹5,000 crores, New Markets (Indian After Market + Export) at 40% of revenue, 40% ROCE and 50% dividend payout.
- The Owen Springs acquisition is funded from "Internal accruals" with "No external debt; no equity dilution".
- Consideration of approximately ₹25 Cr / £2.00 mn buys the entire issued share capital (100%) from OSL Group Holdings.
- Shareholding as on 30.06.2026 is unchanged from 31.03.2026: Promoters 50%, Institutional Investors 13%, Bodies Corporate 2%, Individual & Others 35%.
- Strategic intent behind the mix shift: "deepening our focus on New Markets ... empowers us to maintain steady performance not only in periods of economic expansion, but also remain stable and reliable, no matter the macro environment."
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- "From our beginnings in 1954 to market leadership today, JAI is India's largest and a global leader in tapered and parabolic leaf springs — with a growing portfolio that now includes lift axles and suspension systems, trusted by major OEMs."
- Marquee customer list spans Tata Motors, Ashok Leyland, Bharat Benz, VE Commercial Vehicles, Mahindra, Fuso, Volvo, Force Motors, ISUZU, SCANIA, SML Isuzu, TADANO Escort and UD Trucks.
- Infrastructure moat framed on four pillars: proximity (plants located near key OEM hubs), scale ("Low cost producer with economies of scale"), R&D (in-house centre for product design and testing) and distribution ("Pan-India aftermarket network with digital integration").
- Credit standing cited as CARE A1+/AA and ICRA A1+/AA (Stable) under "SOUND CREDIT PROFILE".
- Innovation firsts claimed: "First to Introduce Parabolic Spring for Indian Roads" and "First to start Leaf Spring Design Centre in India".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Owen Springs is "An established British spring brand, incorporated in 2004 and built over two decades, based at Rotherham, in UK" with 350+ SKUs across commercial vehicles, heritage rail, agricultural equipment and classic vehicles, ~250 distributors/retailers/garages with local warehousing, and a target's-own-estimate UK aftermarket spring share of approximately 8%.
- [Digital] Digital transformation stack spans front-end (Mechanic App, RLP App, JAI Connect, ERP WhatsApp Bot), core operations (Dealer Portal, VTS, ERP-Banking, DMS) and analytics (Tableau BI for real-time decision making across functions).
- [IP] 140+ copyrighted designs across springs and suspension products, patents for air suspension systems (including trailer applications), and the "JAI" trademark registered in 16 countries.
- [Governance] Board committees cover Audit, Nomination & Remuneration, Stakeholders Relationship and a CSR & ESG Committee, with a Risk Management Committee, internal audit, risk dashboards and real-time escalation protocols.
- [Industry] Deck cites SIAM data for the quarter: LCV production up 21% YoY but down 8% QoQ; M&HCV production up 6% YoY but down 29% QoQ, with the demand outlook "Positive supported by sustained infrastructure investments and favorable economic conditions".
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions Jamna Auto as "India's Pioneer & Market Leader in Automotive Suspension Solutions" — India's largest and a global leader in tapered and parabolic leaf springs, founded 1954, now broadening from springs into lift axles and integrated suspension systems while pushing aftermarket and exports under its "LAKSHYA RISE 5000" framework and making its first overseas acquisition.
